summary: Each round a shared pool of dice is sorted onto action spaces, and players draft from them in turn order to gather resources, hire staff, and serve hotel guests who demand specific resource sets for points. It's a brisk, tense efficiency puzzle where you're constantly weighing a cheap-but-picked-over die against an expensive one that does exactly what you need.
praised: clever dice-drafting that gives everyone access to any value at a cost
fast turns keep the game moving
good variety from staff and guest cards each session
criticised: largely multiplayer solitaire outside of dice-drafting order
dice and card luck can swing outcomes
fiddly bookkeeping of resources and tracks
theme feels bolted onto an abstract optimization engine

interaction.detail: The dice pool and turn order are shared and taking a die before an opponent can is the main way you affect them, but each player serves guests and builds their hotel on an entirely separate personal board.

scoring.how_you_win: After a set number of rounds tracked on the round track, the player with the most points from served guests, floor bonuses, and emperor favor wins.
